title: Frequency and Effectiveness of Rehabilitation Programme Interventions Provided in Prison, Drug Rehabilitation Centres and Halfway Houses
what_it_is: Frequency and Effectiveness of Rehabilitation Programme Interventions Provided in Prison, Drug Rehabilitation Centres and Halfway Houses

sections.label: Factors for intervention programme allocation
sections.summary: Inmate risk of re-offending, rehabilitation needs, prison conduct and remaining sentence length are considered when allocating intervention programmes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Factors, such as the inmates’ risk of re-offending, rehabilitation needs, conduct in prison and remaining length of the sentence, are taken into consideration in the allocation of intervention programmes.

sections.label: Halfway house programme sessions
sections.summary: At halfway houses, supervisees undergo an 11-session programme, usually within four months, reinforcing skills and concepts learnt in prison.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: At these halfway houses, supervisees undergo a programme to reinforce the skills and concepts learnt in prison to cope with challenges in the community.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: This programme comprises 11 sessions, usually conducted within four months.

sections.label: SPS inmate programme assessment
sections.summary: SPS assesses inmates using factors including re-offending risk, rehabilitation needs, remaining sentence and responsivity; about half of 2021 admissions suited psychology-based and family programmes, and about 40% attended skills training.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: As I have shared earlier, SPS assesses inmates for programmes based on various factors, such as their risks of re-offending, rehabilitation needs and the remaining length of sentence and also looking at their responsivity with regard to the programmes that are available.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: So, we assess that psychology-based correctional programmes and family programmes would be suitable for about half of the 2021 admissions into prisons.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: About 40% of the inmate population as at end-2021 attended skills training.

sections.label: Requests for rehabilitative programmes
sections.summary: Every request is assessed and considered, inmates are proposed useful programmes, and a throughcare approach runs from prison term start through community release.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: So, I am wondering whether those who are classified in that way as being less likely to be rehabilitated, can also demonstrate, through acts of good faith, through requests, that they are open to attending these rehabilitative programmes and get access to them, if they demonstrate that.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: And I would like to share with the House that every request that we see, we will assess it, consider it and we will also propose to the inmates what will be useful for them.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: In fact, we adopt a throughcare approach where the process of rehabilitation begins when the inmates start their prison term, all the way, with the community, at the end of it.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: And even after the release into the community, SPS still continues to engage the ex-inmates and their families.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: So, we will look at all the different requests and we do our best to provide them the opportunities to be rehabilitated and reintegrated into the community.
